assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a rare complete arc from hormone discovery to transformative drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large, durable clinical and societal impact and cardiovascular and renal benefits now documented in large trials.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinotrophic and receptor actions, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide) are plausible decisive contributors; Knudsen's drug development is industrial and could be seen as technology. Habener and others outside the credited list also matter, so the three-person limit forces contested choices.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is extensive across independent trials and approvals, and clinical use is widespread; recognition is clearly timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should go to physiology/discovery or to drug development is unresolved.
Credit for the peptide identification versus the physiology is contested and I cannot verify priority details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapeutics; the conceptual and clinical impact on immuno-oncology is major.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design and costimulation), June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, early gene-marked and engineered T cells) form a reasonable configuration, though Eshhar, Kuwana, Brenner and others contributed and are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multi-year follow-up give strong confirmation; limits in solid tumours and toxicity are still being addressed, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Eshhar and other early CAR pioneers are not credited here, so the allocation is incomplete.
Long-term safety, secondary malignancy and solid-tumour efficacy remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control with light and transformed circuit biology; the originality and methodological reach are exceptional, though direct medical impact is still emerging.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann established channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel, and Deisseroth plus Boyden brought it to neurons and behaviour. Bamberg, Miesenböck and Boyden are also strong claimants, so six credited people cannot fit into three laureates fairly.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated across labs and species with decades of use; clinical applications such as vision restoration are early, but the tool's maturity as a discovery is high.
uncertainties: Allocation among six credited people is highly contested.
Medical rather than technical impact remains limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing TNF as a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and proving benefit of blockade established cytokine-targeted therapy and changed outcomes in several inflammatory diseases; as an autoimmunity physician I weigh the impact heavily but try not to let field familiarity inflate it.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini carried out the decisive concept and clinical proof, with a clean two-person configuration; the roles of antibody developers and other TNF researchers (such as the cachectin and TNF cloning work) are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with several approved agents and decades of confirmatory evidence; recognition is arguably overdue and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as an already-recognized therapeutic area given its Lasker recognition is uncertain.
The credit of upstream TNF discovery versus therapy is not resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Linking HER2 amplification to aggressive breast cancer and showing that antibody blockade benefits patients was a paradigm for target-directed, biomarker-selected cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Ullrich (HER2/neu cloning and overexpression), Slamon (clinical correlation and trial leadership) and Shepard (antibody development) together cover the discovery-to-drug chain; other contributors such as Weinberg and Hudziak are outside the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with survival benefit in large randomized trials and a durable therapeutic class including later HER2 agents.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers a more fundamental oncogene discovery framing is uncertain.
Priority among the antibody and gene groups is complex and I have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining the thymus-dependent T lineage and bursa-dependent B lineage established the foundation of adaptive immunity and underpins vaccines, immunodeficiency diagnosis and immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Miller (thymic function and T cells) and Cooper (B-cell lineage, with Good and Gabrielsen in the chicken bursa work) fit a two-person split, though Robert Good and others make the historical attribution incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is thoroughly confirmed and textbook; the main concern is that timing is very late and some key contributors have died.
uncertainties: Deceased pioneers such as Good cannot be recognised, which weakens the attribution story.
The age of the discoveries makes timeliness a question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as the founding anti-apoptotic regulator, from the t(14;18) translocation to the cell-death pathway and venetoclax, is a coherent basic-to-clinical story with major impact on cancer biology and therapy.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams drove the family characterisation and mouse genetics; Vaux contributed the early demonstration that BCL-2 blocks cell death. Strasser is a major later contributor, and Tsujimoto and others, who are not credited, are important to the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with robust confirmation and approved BH3-mimetic drugs, though the apoptosis field already received the 2002 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize may reduce appetite.
Priority of the translocation cloning versus the function is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines prevent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level reductions in precancer and cancer now being shown; the public health value is very high.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach and Frazer co-developed the VLP technology; Zhou and others are also involved and zur Hausen's HPV discovery has already been recognised, so credit in the vaccine chain is contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong real-world confirmation across multiple countries, with cancer-incidence data increasing steadily; timing is favourable.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among the VLP groups are unresolved and I cannot verify them.
Zur Hausen's earlier prize may influence the committee's view of novelty.
